body.title: Default clone link-mode on macOS causes ~17s syspolicyd rescan on every venv recreate
body.body:
### Summary

On macOS, the default `--link-mode clone` creates new inodes for every `.so` file on each `uv pip install`. macOS syspolicyd (Gatekeeper) caches its security scan results per-inode, so every venv recreate triggers a full rescan of all native extensions — adding ~17s of wall time for a typical data science stack (pandas, polars, pyarrow, jupyterlab).

`--link-mode hardlink` avoids this because hardlinks share the uv cache's inodes, and syspolicyd recognizes them as already scanned.
## Reproduction

```bash
# Install a typical data-science stack
uv venv && VIRTUAL_ENV=.venv uv pip install pandas polars pyarrow jupyterlab

# First import — slow (~18s), expected
time .venv/bin/python -c "import pandas, polars, pyarrow"

# Second import — fast (~1s), syspolicyd cache warm
time .venv/bin/python -c "import pandas, polars, pyarrow"

# Delete and recreate with clone (default) — slow again (~18s)
rm -rf .venv
uv venv && VIRTUAL_ENV=.venv uv pip install pandas polars pyarrow jupyterlab
time .venv/bin/python -c "import pandas, polars, pyarrow"

# Delete and recreate with hardlink — FAST (~5s)
rm -rf .venv
uv venv && VIRTUAL_ENV=.venv uv pip install --link-mode hardlink pandas polars pyarrow jupyterlab
time .venv/bin/python -c "import pandas, polars, pyarrow"
```

## Root cause

1. `uv pip install` with `--link-mode clone` (default on macOS) uses `clonefile()`, which shares storage blocks but **creates a new inode** per file
2. When Python `dlopen()`s a `.so` with an inode syspolicyd hasn't seen, it performs a full security assessment (YARA scan, code signature check)
3. Unsigned `.so` files (all pip packages) trigger `errSecCSUnsigned` (-67062) and a full scan per file
4. Results are cached per-inode — but clone gives every install new inodes, defeating the cache

With `--link-mode hardlink`, the venv's `.so` files share the inode with uv's global cache. Deleting and recreating the venv reuses the same cache archive entry → same inodes → syspolicyd sees them as already scanned.

## Evidence: hardlink vs clone comparison

Tested with `uv pip install buckaroo jupyterlab polars` (108 packages, 112 `.so` files).
Monitoring `log stream --predicate 'process == "syspolicyd"'` during each import:

```
Run                                      Time     syspolicyd lines   Sample inode
A: clone, fresh install                 19.60s    3391               13301980
B: clone, delete + reinstall            18.57s    3306               13320671  (different inode)
C: hardlink, fresh install               6.14s     175               12783585
D: hardlink, delete + reinstall          5.48s     175               12783585  (same inode)
```

Clone reinstall (B) triggers a full rescan every time — new inodes, ~3300 syspolicyd log lines, ~19s.
Hardlink reinstall (D) reuses the cache's inodes — syspolicyd sees them as already scanned, ~5s.

## Per-package breakdown

Each package tested individually in a fresh clone-mode venv (cold syspolicyd),
then immediately re-imported (warm). Delta = time attributable to syspolicyd.

```
Package         Cold      Warm     Delta    .so count   .so total size
bare python    0.04s     0.03s     0.01s       10          21.1M
polars         2.43s     0.05s     2.38s        1         147.1M
pyarrow        2.47s     0.05s     2.42s       37         105.3M
pandas         9.63s     0.17s     9.46s       45          16.2M
numpy          0.46s     0.03s     0.43s       19           6.9M
jupyterlab     3.30s     0.55s     2.75s        0           0B
ALL TOGETHER  17.70s     1.02s    16.68s
```

Key observations:
- **bare python startup adds ~0s** — Python's own `.so` files live in the persistent uv-managed installation, not cloned per-venv, so they're only scanned once ever.
- **pandas is the biggest offender (9.46s / 57%)** despite only 16MB of `.so` files. It has 45 individual `.so` files, each triggering a separate syspolicyd assessment.
- **Number of `.so` files matters more than total size.** pandas (45 files, 16MB) costs 4x more than polars (1 file, 147MB).
- **jupyterlab has 0 `.so` files itself** but 2.75s delta — its deps (zmq, tornado, etc.) have native extensions.

## Relationship to existing issues

- **#9666** — attributed first-run lag to missing bytecode compilation. `--compile-bytecode` only addresses ~1s of the ~17s overhead; the remaining ~16s is syspolicyd.
- **#12904** — reporter showed `--compile-bytecode` doesn't fix the ~16s first run, consistent with syspolicyd being the dominant factor. Root cause was never identified.
- **#16726 / #16003** — Gatekeeper SIGKILL of unsigned Python interpreters. Related mechanism (syspolicyd) but different symptom (SIGKILL vs slow scan of `.so` extensions).

## Possible fixes

1. **Document the workaround.** `UV_LINK_MODE=hardlink` eliminates the rescan on reinstalls. This is a one-line config change for users.
2. **Consider changing the macOS default to `hardlink`.** The current rationale for `clone` on macOS is CoW efficiency on APFS, but hardlinks are equally storage-efficient (no data duplication) and avoid the syspolicyd penalty. The safety concern (modifying a hardlinked file corrupts the cache) only applies to the `RECORD` file, which already gets special treatment.
3. **Hybrid approach.** Use hardlink for `.so`/`.dylib` files specifically, clone for everything else.

## References

- [uv `LinkMode` default implementation](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/crates/uv-fs/src/link.rs) — macOS/iOS/Linux default to `Clone`, others to `Hardlink`
- [uv `--link-mode` docs](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/settings/#link-mode)
- [syspolicyd YARA scanning on first launch](https://lapcatsoftware.com/articles/2024/2/3.html) — documents syspolicyd scanning behavior and per-inode caching
- [APFS clonefile() creates new inodes](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1585689-clonefile) — Apple docs confirming clones get distinct metadata (inodes)
- [#9666 — Noticeable lag with uv-created virtual environments during first interpreter session](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/9666) — attributed to missing bytecode compilation, syspolicyd not investigated
- [#12904 — Expected Impact of --compile-bytecode](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/12904) — `--compile-bytecode` doesn't explain the ~16s first-run overhead
- [#16726 — UV Python SIGKILL Issue on macOS](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/16726) — Gatekeeper SIGKILL of unsigned binaries via `com.apple.provenance` xattr
- [#16003 — macOS code signing workaround](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/16003) — `codesign --force -s -` workaround
- [PR #18280 — Apple Developer ID signing of release binaries](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/18280) — in-progress fix for signing uv's own binaries


Note the timings are on a Macbook Pro M4 Pro 48 GB of Ram

### Platform

Darwin 25.0.0 arm64

### Version

uv 0.10.11 (006b56b12 2026-03-16)

### Python version

Python 3.13.11
